newsitem.title: UK: UK's Eastern announces new gas sales code.
newsitem.headline: UK's Eastern announces new gas sales code.

text.p: Eastern Natural Gas (ENG), a unit of Hanson Plc, said on Monday it has introduced a new code of conduct on doorstep selling of domestic natural gas supplies in Britain.
The new code follows complaints from industry regulator Ofgas last week that customers were being misinformed or pressurised into signing contracts.

Under the code, Eastern is to contact all customers who have already signed agreements to confirm that they still wish to be supplied with gas by the company. And Eastern will extend the "cooling off" period, during which customers can cancel contracts with no obligations, to 14 days from seven days from the date of signing.

The code also stipulates that all new customers will be contacted by phone or letter within the extended cooling off period to make sure they have understood the process. Eastern says that for customers who have doubts or concerns about switching supplier, the company will give them "every assistance" to allow then to return to their original supplier.

The code of conduct is a response to complaints from customers in two pilot areas of Britain where domestic gas supply is being deregulated. From April 29 this year, customers in the south western counties of Devon, Cornwall and Somerset have been able to buy gas from any licensed supplier, of whom there are now 11, instead of just from former monopoly holder British Gas Plc.
And from February 10 next year, Dorset and the former county of Avon will open for competition, with Kent and East and West Sussex following on March 7.
The new markets have led to a wide range of marketing techniques, ranging from television advertising to telephone marketing and door to door selling.

Eastern said in a statement on Monday that "during the eight months since the pilot areas opened for competition, ENG has visited almost 250,000 potential customers -- 35,000 of whom have agreed to switch from British Gas to ENG.
"Throughout this period ENG has received 11 complaints from Ofgas -- all of which have been thoroughly investigated and resolved. In most cases, sales people have been dismissed."
Of Eastern's new customers, around 7,500 are in the first pilot area, with the remaining 27,500 in the second pilot area where the company has been marketing since October 7.

Clare Spottiswoode, Director General of Ofgas, said "surveys by Ofgas and the Gas Consumers Council have shown that doorstep selling is welcomed by many customers because it helps them to understand how gas competition works. But it is essential that it is done well.
"We will be monitoring Eastern's new code along with the performance of all other suppliers to achieve the highest standards in the expanding competitive market."

A spokesman for Ofgas said last week that British Gas is losing customers to other suppliers at the rate of 2,000 a week in the first pilot area, and he expected that a total of 100,000 out of a little over 500,000 in the pilot area will have switched by the end of the year.
The whole of Britain, including nearly 19 million households, will be opened to competition during 1998.
